item.title: Correction · The owner identified that DataSF's Assessor Parcel dataset gives Chase Center (formerly tracked as status.csv blklot 8722025) and the neighboring Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 office towers (formerly blklot 8722063) byte-identical geometry -- one shared master-condominium-association land parcel spanning the whole Mission Bay South Blocks 29-32 superblock (confirmed: Chase Center, both Uber towers, a parking structure and a small broadcast building are all separate condo units on one shared plat). This made the two records' polygons fully overlapping on the map -- a click anywhere in the shared area could resolve to either record, and each record's own "Where it is" mini-map showed the wrong footprint. Migrated both records off status.csv onto hand-derived, non-overlapping real geometry: Chase Center (record_id mission_bay_chase_center) is now the full Assessor parcel with both Uber towers' own real OpenStreetMap building footprints subtracted out; Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 (record_id mission_bay_uber_3_4) is now the union of those same two real OSM footprints. The owner also identified that Harmonic Brewing's own standalone taproom building, at the NE edge of the site (7 Warriors Way Ste 206, confirmed via its own DataSF business-registration address and geocoded location), and Miller & Lux (7 Warriors Way Ste 208, confirmed inside the arena's own footprint) are both Chase Center/Thrive City tenants, not separate structures -- Harmonic Brewing's building is included in Chase Center's new geometry (it falls within the parcel-minus-Uber-towers remainder) rather than tracked as a separate record. Re-running the retail spatial join (src/join_retail.py) against the corrected geometry surfaced three more real, previously-untracked Thrive City tenants -- Cupcakin' Bake Shop, Siren Cafe & Bar and The Sarap Shop -- added separately; see those changelog rows.

item.title: Added · Parklab Gardens & Mission Bay Commons (interim, west): The owner asked whether the P12/P13/P15 sources (the interim parcels hosting Spark Social SF, Stagecoach Greens and Urban Sprouts) included SF Rec & Park's own community-workshop decks. They didn't yet; added all three, each verified by fetching the PDF directly. Community Meeting #3 (Apr 29, 2025, 83 pages) has individually labeled concept-plan pages for P12, P13 and P15 -- food trucks, outdoor dining and a pavilion on P15, matching Spark Social SF's current use; soccer pitches and outdoor fitness on P12 -- plus an alternative option for P12. Design-workshop concepts, not an adopted final plan: the design team was only selected via an Aug 2025 OCII/MBDG RFQ, after Workshop 3.
